sourcedFrom: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. (UNDATED — nothing in the document states one)
cleanIntro: A .357 Magnum Kimber revolver cleans with the cylinder swung out and nothing taken apart — Kimber says outright that it does not need to be disassembled for cleaning, and forbids going inside. Bore, chambers, the two cylinder faces and the extractor are the whole job.

steps.title: Finger outside the guard before the cylinder moves
steps.action: Keep your finger outside the trigger guard and the muzzle pointed somewhere harmless the entire time the cylinder is being opened and emptied. On a revolver the trigger turns the cylinder, so a finger inside the guard during unloading is the one thing that can turn a clearing into a discharge.
steps.quote: Never place your finger inside the trigger guard or on the trigger when unloading your revolver.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Loading / Unloading K6s, K6s (DASA), & K6xs, printed p.26-28

steps.title: Cylinder release, and the cylinder swings LEFT
steps.action: Depress the cylinder release and push the cylinder out of the frame from right to left. If it resists, the hammer is back or the action is not at rest — forcing a cylinder against a locked bolt damages the crane and the hand.
steps.quote: Depress the cylinder release and push the cylinder open from right to left.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — OPERATION — Loading / Unloading K6s, K6s (DASA), & K6xs, printed p.26-28

steps.title: Every chamber emptied and checked, by eye and by finger
steps.action: Work the extractor rod to lift the cases clear, take them out, then look through every chamber and run a fingertip across the rear face. A case left in a chamber you did not look at is the failure this step exists for.
steps.quote: Always make sure the firearm is unloaded before cleaning.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — SAFETY — Rules of Firearm Safety, printed p.8

steps.title: ⛔ It does not come apart — Kimber says so
steps.action: There is no field strip on this revolver and there is not meant to be. Kimber states that it does not need to be disassembled for cleaning and lubrication, and separately forbids manipulating the internals at all. Everything below is done with the cylinder open.
steps.aside: Do not disassemble your revolver or manipulate its internal components.
steps.quote: Your revolver does not need to be disassembled for purposes of cleaning and lubrication.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — Preventative maintenance K6s, K6s (DASA), & K6xs, printed p.36-37

steps.title: Bore: wet patch, soak, wet brush chamber-to-muzzle
steps.action: Run a solvent-wet patch through the barrel and let it work for a few minutes, then a wet bore brush from the chamber end out the muzzle, several passes. If you are using a rod, thread the brush on AFTER the rod is through the barrel and pull it out the muzzle — that keeps the brush from being dragged back across the forcing cone.
steps.aside: Note: when using a cleaning rod, attach the bore brush after the rod is inserted through the barrel, then pull the brush through the barrel and out the muzzle.
steps.quote: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel and out the muzzle, making several passes.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — Cleaning & Lubrication, printed p.38

steps.title: Chambers: same method, but rod in from the BREECH end
steps.action: Clean each chamber the way you cleaned the bore, with one difference Kimber prints in capitals — the rod goes in from the breech end of the chambers, not the front. Do every chamber, and pay attention to the mouths, where the fouling ring that makes cases stick forms.
steps.quote: Clean the cylinder using the same method as the barrel EXCEPT insert the cleaning rod into the breech end of the chambers.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — Cleaning & Lubrication, printed p.38

steps.title: Cylinder faces, extractor and breech face — then take the oil back off
steps.action: Clean both faces of the cylinder and the extractor, then wipe the excess cleaner and lubricant off the chambers, the cylinder faces and the breech face with a clean patch. That last wipe is not tidiness: oil left on those surfaces reaches the cartridges and can penetrate primers.
steps.quote: To reduce oil and solvent contamination of cartridges, use a clean patch to remove excess cleaner and lubricant from the chambers, the front and rear faces of the cylinder and the breech face.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — Preventative maintenance K6s, K6s (DASA), & K6xs, printed p.36-37

steps.title: Exterior wiped, and nothing near an ultrasonic tank
steps.action: Wipe all exterior surfaces clean and lightly oiled. Keep night sights out of ultrasonic cleaners entirely — Kimber says ultrasonic cleaning is not recommended at all and that damage from it is not covered.
steps.quote: Wipe off all dirt on all exterior surfaces of the revolver.
steps.cite: Kimber revolver Models Safety & Instruction Manual — Safety & Instruction Manual, 25pp. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book. — CARE — Cleaning & Lubrication, printed p.38

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for this revolver and Kimber does not publish one. Its own words are "Your revolver does not need to be disassembled for purposes of cleaning and lubrication", followed by "Do not disassemble your revolver or manipulate its internal components. Doing so could affect its safety, reliability and performance". A manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other source, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else and the absence is recorded.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Wet patch, soak, wet brush chamber-to-muzzle, several passes
Attach the brush after the rod is through, and pull it out the muzzle
Light oil, then a dry patch before shooting

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS
tasks: ⛔ Rod in from the BREECH end of the chambers — the opposite of the bore
Every chamber, and work the mouths where the fouling ring forms
Wipe the excess back off so nothing reaches the cartridges

cleaning.name: CYLINDER FACES & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Both faces of the cylinder and the extractor
Breech face wiped clean and dry

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe all dirt off; light oil
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning, and never with night sights fitted

reassembly: Nothing was taken apart — there is nothing to reassemble, and that is by design.
Swing the cylinder gently back into the frame and confirm it locks in place.
Run a dry patch through the bore and every chamber to take the oil back out before loading.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Cylinder closed and latched, chambers proven empty, muzzle safe. Open and close the cylinder a few times and feel it seat and lock without drag. Then, still empty, run the action through a full double-action stroke slowly and watch the cylinder carry up and lock before the hammer falls. Let the trigger return fully forward between strokes — Kimber is explicit that the trigger must fully reset or the revolver will not function properly. Anything late, gritty or loose goes to Kimber rather than the range.
